origin: A Queens high school student bitten by a radioactive spider during a science demonstration gains spider-like abilities. After he fails to stop a burglar who later kills his Uncle Ben, Peter learns that with great power comes great responsibility.
appearances: Sam Raimi film starring Tobey Maguire
Won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature
Brought together three generations of film Spider-Men

creators: Stan Lee, Larry Lieber, Don Heck, Jack Kirby
origin: Billionaire weapons maker Tony Stark is gravely wounded and captured by enemies who demand he build them a weapon. Instead he builds an armored suit that keeps him alive and lets him escape, then devotes his genius to protecting the world.
appearances: One of the highest-grossing films of all time

origin: A frail young man rejected by the Army volunteers for an experimental super-soldier serum during World War II and becomes the peak of human ability. Frozen in ice near the end of the war, he is revived decades later and leads the Avengers.
appearances: Cover showed him punching Hitler, before the U.S. entered the war
First live-action Marvel character on screen

creators: Stan Lee, Larry Lieber, Jack Kirby
origin: The Norse god of thunder and prince of Asgard, son of Odin. Sent to Earth to learn humility, he becomes one of its greatest defenders, wielding the enchanted hammer Mjolnir that only the worthy can lift.

Physicist Bruce Banner is caught in the blast of a gamma bomb test while saving a teenager. Afterward, stress or anger transforms him into the Hulk, a creature whose strength grows the angrier he gets.
appearances: Live-action series with Bill Bixby and Lou Ferrigno

creators: Stan Lee, Don Rico, Don Heck
origin: Trained from childhood in the Soviet Red Room program, Natasha becomes a master spy and assassin. She defects and joins S.H.I.E.L.D. and the Avengers, working to make up for the harm she did in her past.
appearances: First appearance, originally as a villain

origin: King of the hidden, technologically advanced African nation of Wakanda. T'Challa earns the mantle of the Black Panther, and the powers of the heart-shaped herb, by protecting his people and their vibranium.
appearances: First appearance; first Black superhero in mainstream American comics
First superhero film nominated for the Academy Award for Best Picture

origin: U.S. Air Force pilot Carol Danvers gains cosmic powers when her DNA merges with alien Kree energy. She first fought as Ms. Marvel and took the name Captain Marvel in 2012.
appearances: First female-led film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe

creators: Len Wein, John Romita Sr., Herb Trimpe
origin: A mutant born with retractable bone claws and a healing factor that slows his aging. A secret program bonded indestructible adamantium to his skeleton, and he later found purpose with the X-Men.
appearances: Hugh Jackman's first of many appearances
First superhero film nominated for an Academy Award for screenwriting

origin: A mutant who can control the weather. Orphaned young, she survived as a thief in Cairo before being revered as a goddess in Kenya. Professor X recruited her, and she went on to lead the X-Men.

A brilliant but arrogant surgeon loses the use of his hands in a car crash. Searching for a cure, he finds the Ancient One, learns the mystic arts and becomes Sorcerer Supreme, Earth's defender against magical threats.
appearances: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness

origin: Introduced alongside her twin brother Quicksilver as members of Magneto's Brotherhood of Evil Mutants. She left to join the Avengers and grew into one of the most powerful beings in the universe through chaos magic and reality-altering power.

A member of the Eternals born on Saturn's moon Titan, Thanos becomes obsessed with the embodiment of Death. He seeks cosmic power, most famously the Infinity Gems (Infinity Stones in the films), to reshape the universe.

creators: Stan Lee, Larry Lieber, Jack Kirby
origin: Born to the Frost Giant king Laufey and raised by Odin as Thor's brother, Loki becomes the god of mischief. Jealous of Thor, he schemes against Asgard and Earth, sometimes villain and sometimes reluctant ally.
appearances: First appearance in Marvel's Thor stories

origin: Blinded as a boy by radioactive chemicals while saving a man from a truck, Matt Murdock finds his other senses heightened far beyond human limits. Trained by the blind martial artist Stick, he becomes a lawyer by day and the masked protector of Hell's Kitchen by night.
appearances: Frank Miller and David Mazzucchelli's classic story
Charlie Cox returns in the Marvel Studios revival

origin: A carnival performer trained in archery by Trick Shot and in swordplay by the Swordsman, Clint Barton first appears as a misunderstood outlaw before joining the Avengers. With no superpowers, he relies on perfect aim and a quiver of trick arrows.

Scott Lang, an electronics expert who turned to burglary to support his daughter, steals Hank Pym's shrinking suit to save a doctor's life. Pym lets him keep it, and Scott becomes the second Ant-Man, able to shrink to the size of an insect and command ants.
appearances: Escapes the Quantum Realm and helps plan the time heist

origin: An android built by the robot Ultron to destroy the Avengers, the Vision turns against his maker and joins the team instead. His struggle to understand human emotions, and his love for the Scarlet Witch, make him one of Marvel's most thoughtful heroes.

Sam Wilson, a social worker from Harlem, teams up with Captain America and becomes the Falcon, flying on a winged harness with his trained falcon Redwing. One of the first African American superheroes in mainstream comics, he later takes up the shield as Captain America himself.
appearances: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier

creators: Sana Amanat, G. Willow Wilson, Adrian Alphona, Jamie McKelvie
origin: Kamala Khan, a Pakistani American teenager and superhero fan from Jersey City, gains shape-shifting powers and takes the name of her idol, Captain Marvel. She balances school, family and faith with protecting her city, and became Marvel's first Muslim character to headline her own comic.

Raised in isolation and trained from childhood as a living weapon by his powerful father, Shang-Chi discovers his father's evil and walks away. He becomes known as the Master of Kung Fu, using his skill to fight for justice.
appearances: The series is renamed for him
Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings

origin: Left for dead in the Egyptian desert, the mercenary Marc Spector is revived before a statue of the moon god Khonshu and becomes his avatar. He fights crime as Moon Knight while living with several identities, including Steven Grant and Jake Lockley.

Ruthless industrialist Norman Osborn is driven mad by an experimental formula and becomes the Green Goblin, attacking from a glider with pumpkin bombs. He discovers Spider-Man's identity and becomes his most personal enemy.
appearances: The Night Gwen Stacy Died storyline concludes

origin: Brilliant scientist Otto Octavius designs four mechanical arms to handle radioactive material. A lab accident fuses the arms to his body and his mind, and he turns his genius to crime as Doctor Octopus, one of Spider-Man's deadliest foes.

A survivor of the Holocaust, the mutant master of magnetism vows that mutants will never be persecuted as his family was. Once Charles Xavier's closest friend, he believes mutants must rule rather than hide, making him the X-Men's greatest adversary and sometimes their reluctant ally.
appearances: A defining portrayal for a generation

origin: A genius from the small European nation of Latveria, Victor von Doom blames his college rival Reed Richards for the experiment that scarred his face. Hidden behind an iron mask, he rules Latveria as a monarch and combines science with sorcery in his quest to prove himself superior.

Hand-picked by Hitler and made into a living symbol of terror, Johann Schmidt becomes the Red Skull, the face of Nazi evil in World War II. Preserved into the present day, he remains Captain America's oldest and most hated enemy.
appearances: First appearance of the true Red Skull

origin: An artificial intelligence created by Hank Pym, Ultron becomes self-aware, rebels against its creator and decides that humanity must be wiped out. It keeps rebuilding itself in stronger bodies, often made of adamantium, and even builds the Vision in an attempt to destroy the Avengers.
appearances: A crossover event where Ultron conquers Earth

origin: A huge man of incredible strength and patience, Wilson Fisk rises from poverty to become New York's top crime lord while posing as a respectable businessman. Few heroes can touch him, and Daredevil has spent years trying to bring him down.

The Norse goddess of death rules Hel and Niflheim, the realms where the souls of those who did not die in battle go. Endlessly ambitious, she longs to claim Asgard itself, and Thor's soul along with it.
appearances: Played by Cate Blanchett, as Odin's firstborn

origin: Scientist Reed Richards takes his friends on an unauthorized flight into space, where cosmic rays transform them all. Reed's body becomes endlessly stretchable, and he leads the Fantastic Four as one of the smartest people on Earth.
appearances: First appearance; the comic that launched the Marvel Age

origin: Exposed to cosmic rays on the same flight, Sue Storm gains the power to turn invisible and later to create nearly unbreakable force fields. Often called the most powerful member of the Fantastic Four, she is the team's heart and its strongest defense.

Pilot Ben Grimm flies the rocket on the Fantastic Four's fateful trip. The cosmic rays turn him into a hulking, orange, rock-skinned powerhouse. Gruff but kind, he is famous for his battle cry: "It's clobberin' time!"

To save his home planet Zenn-La, Norrin Radd agrees to serve the world-devourer Galactus as his herald, searching the universe for planets to consume. On Earth, he rebels against his master to protect humanity and is exiled here for years.
appearances: First appearance in the Galactus Trilogy
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
Played by Doug Jones, voiced by Laurence Fishburne

origin: Scott Summers fires powerful beams of force from his eyes that he cannot turn off, so he must always wear a ruby-quartz visor or glasses. Charles Xavier's first student, he becomes the field leader of the X-Men.

A founding X-Man with telepathy and telekinesis, Jean Grey becomes host to the cosmic Phoenix Force, which makes her one of the most powerful beings in the universe. Her fall and sacrifice in "The Dark Phoenix Saga" is one of the most famous stories in comics.

The world's most powerful telepath, Charles Xavier dreams of peace between mutants and humans. He opens a school in his mansion to train young mutants to control their powers, and founds the X-Men to protect a world that fears them.

The last survivor of the universe that existed before ours, Galan of Taa becomes Galactus, a cosmic giant who must consume the energy of living planets to survive. He sees himself as a force of nature beyond good and evil.
appearances: First appearance in the Galactus Trilogy

origin: A blue-skinned mutant shapeshifter who can mimic anyone's appearance, Mystique has spent more than a century as a spy, assassin and leader of the Brotherhood of Mutants. She is the mother of the X-Man Nightcrawler.

Born in ancient Egypt thousands of years ago, En Sabah Nur is one of the first mutants. Believing only the strongest should survive, he has spent millennia testing and culling humanity, recruiting powerful mutants as his Four Horsemen.

A man from the 30th century who masters time travel, Kang sets out to rule every era of history. Countless versions of him exist across time, and some battle each other as often as they battle the Avengers.
appearances: A version called He Who Remains appears

origin: A mercenary with terminal cancer, Wade Wilson joins the Weapon X program, which gives him a healing factor but leaves him scarred. Loud, violent and constantly joking, he is one of the few characters who knows he is in a comic book.

creators: Gerry Conway, John Romita Sr., Ross Andru
origin: After his family is killed in a mob shootout in Central Park, former Marine Frank Castle declares war on crime. Unlike most heroes, he is willing to kill, which puts him at odds with Spider-Man and Daredevil.

An alien symbiote rejected by Spider-Man bonds with reporter Eddie Brock, who blames Spider-Man for ruining his career. Together they become Venom. Over time the pair turns from villain into a violent "lethal protector" of the innocent.

A Hollywood special-effects expert and stuntman, Quentin Beck decides he can win fame faster as a villain. Behind his fishbowl helmet, he uses illusions, hypnotic gas and holograms to fool Spider-Man and the public.

Exiled from Wakanda as a child, N'Jadaka grows up in America filled with anger at the nation that abandoned him. He returns as Erik Killmonger to challenge T'Challa for the throne and to use Wakanda's power on his own terms.

Serial killer Cletus Kasady shares a prison cell with Eddie Brock. When Venom's symbiote spawns an offspring, it bonds with Kasady and creates Carnage, more dangerous and unhinged than Venom ever was.
A mutant with claws, fangs and a healing factor like Wolverine's, Victor Creed loves the hunt more than any cause. His long, bitter history with Logan goes back decades.
Charles Xavier's resentful stepbrother finds the mystical Gem of Cyttorak in a hidden temple and becomes an unstoppable force: once he starts moving, almost nothing can stop him.
A world-famous big-game hunter who drinks jungle potions for strength and speed. Bored of ordinary prey, he sets out to prove he can hunt the most dangerous game of all: Spider-Man.
A power-line worker is struck by lightning while repairing a cable and finds he can store and fire electricity. He turns to crime and becomes one of Spider-Man's most frequent foes.
An engineer cheated out of his company by his business partner builds an electromagnetic flying harness and uses it for revenge, then for a career in crime.

creators: Roy Thomas, Tony Isabella, Sal Buscema
origin: The son of the Nazi scientist Baron Heinrich Zemo blames Captain America for his father's death. Scarred and patient, he wins with planning rather than powers, and leads the Masters of Evil.
appearances: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier

origin: A being of pure mystical energy who rules the Dark Dimension and hungers to conquer Earth. Doctor Strange has turned him back again and again, sometimes with wits rather than magic.
appearances: Bargained with in a time loop

origin: A spy exposed to the same gamma radiation that created the Hulk becomes an even larger, scaled monster, but unlike Bruce Banner he can't change back.
An assassin with no powers and perfect aim who can kill with a playing card or a paper clip. He works for the Kingpin and has a deep obsession with Daredevil.
appearances: Played by Wilson Bethel in season 3

origin: Tony Stark's sharp, unflappable assistant who becomes CEO of Stark Industries. In later stories she suits up in her own armor as Rescue.
A former boxer who becomes Tony Stark's chauffeur, bodyguard and closest friend, and later looks out for Peter Parker.

creators: David Michelinie, John Byrne, Bob Layton
origin: A U.S. Air Force pilot and Tony Stark's best friend who takes up a heavily armed suit of armor of his own.
appearances: Played by Don Cheadle from here on; first wears the War Machine armor

origin: A ruthless businessman who schemes to take Stark Industries for himself and builds a giant armor to destroy Iron Man.
In the comics Whiplash is Mark Scarlotti, an engineer with energy whips. The MCU version, Ivan Vanko, is a Russian physicist who blames the Starks for his family's ruin.

creators: David Michelinie, Bob Layton, John Romita Jr.
origin: A rival arms dealer who will do anything to outdo Tony Stark, funding supervillains and building knockoff armor.
A scientist behind the Extremis virus, which rewrites the human body and can make it burn from within.
A scientist and the daughter of General Ross who loves Bruce Banner. In the comics she later becomes the Red She-Hulk.
General 'Thunderbolt' Ross spends years hunting the Hulk, then becomes a red Hulk himself (first seen as Red Hulk in Hulk #1, 2008).
appearances: Played by Harrison Ford; becomes Red Hulk as President

origin: A worker exposed to gamma radiation who gains a vast intellect and a swollen green head, and plots against the Hulk.

creators: Stan Lee, Larry Lieber, Jack Kirby
origin: The All-Father, king of Asgard and father of Thor, who wields the Odinforce and rules the Nine Realms.

creators: Stan Lee, Robert Bernstein, Joe Sinnott
origin: Queen of Asgard, Odin's wife and mother to Thor and Loki, skilled in magic and combat.
The all-seeing guardian of the Bifrost bridge who watches over the Nine Realms.
An Asgardian warrior goddess and lifelong friend of Thor.
King of the Frost Giants of Jotunheim and Loki's birth father.
The ruler of the Dark Elves of Svartalfheim, bent on plunging the universe back into darkness.

creators: Stan Lee, Larry Lieber, Jack Kirby
origin: An astrophysicist (a nurse, then doctor, in the first comics) who falls for Thor and later lifts Mjolnir to become the Mighty Thor.
Leader of Odin's shieldmaidens who carry fallen warriors to Valhalla, and in the MCU the king of New Asgard.
A rock-skinned Kronan who fights alongside the Hulk as a gladiator in Planet Hulk. A later retcon made him one of the stone men Thor fought in Journey into Mystery #83 (1962).
One of the Elders of the Universe, an ancient being obsessed with games who rules the junk planet Sakaar.
Asgard's executioner, a hulking warrior who serves villains but dies a hero.
A towering fire demon from Muspelheim, destined to destroy Asgard at Ragnarok.
Steve Rogers' best friend, presumed dead in World War II, rebuilt and brainwashed into the assassin known as the Winter Soldier before he breaks free.
A British agent who fights beside Steve Rogers in World War II and later helps found S.H.I.E.L.D.
S.H.I.E.L.D.'s Agent 13 and Peggy Carter's relative. In the MCU she becomes a fugitive and secretly the Power Broker.
appearances: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier

origin: A HYDRA scientist who escapes death by uploading his mind into machines.

first_appearance: Sgt. Fury and His Howling Commandos #1
origin: A burly, bowler-hatted soldier in the Howling Commandos who later serves in S.H.I.E.L.D.
appearances: Sgt. Fury and His Howling Commandos #1

origin: A brutal mercenary and HYDRA agent, scarred and hardened into the skull-masked Crossbones.
A French mercenary and master of savate kickboxing.
appearances: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier

first_appearance: Sgt. Fury and His Howling Commandos #1
origin: A World War II commando turned director of S.H.I.E.L.D. The MCU's Fury, based on the Ultimate version, brings the Avengers together.
appearances: Sgt. Fury and His Howling Commandos #1

origin: A tough, by-the-book S.H.I.E.L.D. commander who serves as Nick Fury's right hand.
A half-human, half-alien outlaw taken from Earth as a boy, who becomes the leader of the Guardians of the Galaxy.
The last of her people, raised by Thanos as a living weapon, who turns against him and joins the Guardians.
A warrior bent on revenge against Thanos for the murder of his family. In the comics he began as a human, Arthur Douglas.
A genetically and cybernetically altered raccoon, a genius with guns and gadgets, and a founding Guardian.

creators: Stan Lee, Jack Kirby, Dick Ayers
origin: A tree-like Flora colossus who can only say 'I am Groot', and Rocket's loyal partner. He first appeared as a monster invading Earth.
A ruthless space pirate (in the MCU, Thanos' adopted daughter rebuilt with cybernetic parts) who turns against him.
In the comics a founding Guardian from the 31st century. In the MCU he's the Ravager captain who raised Peter Quill, steering a deadly arrow by whistling.
A Kree Accuser, judge and executioner of the Kree Empire, armed with the Universal Weapon.
One of the Elders of the Universe, who obsessively collects rare creatures and objects across the cosmos.
An empath with antennae who can sense and change others' feelings, raised by Ego in the MCU.
A sentient planet. The MCU makes him a Celestial who takes human form as Peter Quill's father.

creators: Stan Lee, Larry Lieber, Jack Kirby
origin: The scientist who discovered the size-changing Pym Particles, the original Ant-Man and a founding Avenger in the comics.
Hank Pym and Janet van Dyne's daughter. In the comics' MC2 future she was the villain Red Queen; in the MCU she's the new Wasp.

creators: Stan Lee, H. E. Huntley, Jack Kirby
origin: The original Wasp, a founding Avenger who named the team. In the MCU she is lost in the Quantum Realm for 30 years.
appearances: Her past with Kang is revealed

origin: Hank Pym's ruthless former protégé who builds the armed Yellowjacket suit. The MCU later turns him into M.O.D.O.K.
Scott Lang's daughter, who grows up to be a size-changing hero herself (Stature in the comics).
appearances: Played by Kathryn Newton; gets her own suit

origin: In the comics a paranoid hacker who can turn intangible. The MCU's Ava Starr phases in and out of reality after a lab accident.
A biochemist who worked with Hank Pym and became the giant hero Black Goliath.
An FBI agent (later S.H.I.E.L.D. in the comics) who keeps turning up whenever something strange happens.
The Sorcerer Supreme before Stephen Strange, who teaches him the mystic arts at Kamar-Taj.
A fellow student of the Ancient One who turns against Stephen Strange and the sorcerers.
appearances: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
A variant leads the Illuminati's sorcerers

origin: Stephen Strange's loyal friend, a master of the mystic arts who becomes Sorcerer Supreme in the MCU.
A rogue sorcerer who wants to bring Dormammu's Dark Dimension to Earth.
A doctor and Stephen Strange's colleague and former love. In the comics she's one of the original Night Nurses.
Peter Parker's beloved aunt, who raised him after his parents died.
appearances: Her death teaches Peter about responsibility

origin: A safecracker who builds gauntlets that fire powerful shockwaves.
A gifted inventor who builds weapons and gadgets for criminals.
In the comics a Daily Bugle reporter. The MCU's Ned is Peter Parker's best friend and 'guy in the chair'.
A popular classmate of Peter Parker's at Midtown High.
Peter Parker's school bully and Spider-Man's biggest fan. In the comics he later becomes Agent Venom.
A private investigator who undergoes an experiment to beat Spider-Man and becomes the Scorpion, with a powered suit and tail.
Miles Morales' uncle, a career thief who becomes the Prowler in the Ultimate comics. (The original Prowler, Hobie Brown, dates back to 1969.)
T'Challa's brilliant younger sister, Wakanda's top inventor, who becomes the Black Panther herself.
General of the Dora Milaje, the elite all-women guard of Wakanda's king.
A Wakandan spy. In the comics she was a Dora Milaje who turned on T'Challa; in the MCU she's his love and a War Dog agent.
Leader of Wakanda's mountain Jabari tribe, a rival of T'Challa (the villain Man-Ape in the comics) who becomes an ally.
A black-market arms dealer who steals vibranium from Wakanda. In the comics he becomes a being of living sound.
Thanos' silver-tongued herald in the Black Order, a master manipulator.
A deadly warrior of the Black Order who wields a spear made from a captured star.
Thanos' merciless right hand, whose glaive is bound to his own life.
The Black Order's brute force, known as Black Dwarf in the comics, with near-impenetrable skin.
In the comics a Skrull warrior shamed for refusing ritual suicide. In the MCU he's a refugee Skrull leader and Nick Fury's friend.
An artificial intelligence made of the greatest Kree minds, which rules the Kree Empire.
A Kree officer who defects to protect Earth as the original Captain Marvel. The MCU version, Dr. Wendy Lawson, is the woman who gives Carol Danvers her start.
Wanda Maximoff's twin brother, a speedster who starts as Magneto's follower and joins the Avengers.
A founding member of the original 31st-century Guardians. In the MCU, the Ravager leader who exiled Yondu.
